textbookText: 91. The specific heat capacity of a substance is defined as: A) Heat required to raise the temperature of unit mass of the substance by 1°C (or 1 K) B) Total heat contained in a given mass of substance C) Heat required to melt unit mass of a substance D) Heat lost by a substance while cooling to room temperature
92. The SI unit of specific heat capacity is: A) J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ B) J K⁻¹ C) J kg⁻¹ D) J s⁻¹

93. Water has an unusually high specific heat capacity of about: A) 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, making it excellent for moderating climate and use in cooling systems B) 420 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ C) 42 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ D) 4.2 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹

94. Latent heat of fusion of ice is the heat required to: A) Convert ice to water at 0°C without any change in temperature B) Raise the temperature of ice from 0°C to 100°C C) Convert water to steam at 100°C D) Cool water down to 0°C

95. The principle of calorimetry (method of mixtures) states that, in an isolated system: A) Heat lost by the hot body equals heat gained by the cold body B) Heat lost is always greater than heat gained C) Temperature of both bodies becomes 0°C eventually D) Mass is converted to heat energy
96. Latent heat of vaporization of water at 100°C is approximately: A) 2260 kJ/kg, much larger than its latent heat of fusion B) 336 kJ/kg C) 4.2 kJ/kg D) 22.6 kJ/kg

97. During a change of state (like ice melting), the temperature: A) Remains constant even though heat is continuously absorbed B) Rises steadily as heat is absorbed C) Falls as heat is absorbed D) Increases only after all the substance has melted

98. Water equivalent of a calorimeter is defined as: A) The mass of water that would absorb/release the same heat as the calorimeter for the same temperature change B) The actual mass of water poured into the calorimeter C) The volume of the calorimeter in liters D) The specific heat capacity of the calorimeter material

99. Why does a burn from steam at 100°C tend to be more severe than a burn from boiling water at 100°C (extraordinary fact)? A) Steam releases a large additional latent heat of vaporization (~2260 kJ/kg) upon condensing on skin B) Steam is at a higher temperature than boiling water C) Steam has a lower specific heat than water D) Steam contains more mass than the same volume of water
100. The heat required to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water (specific heat 4200 J/kg·K) by 5 K is: A) 42000 J B) 8400 J C) 21000 J D) 4200 J

101. Which of the following materials would heat up FASTEST for equal mass and equal heat supplied? A) A substance with low specific heat capacity B) A substance with high specific heat capacity C) Water (highest common specific heat) D) A substance with high latent heat only

102. In Regnault's method / method of mixtures to find specific heat of a solid, heat lost by the hot solid equals: A) Heat gained by water and the calorimeter (including stirrer) B) Heat gained by the surrounding air only C) Heat lost by the water D) Zero, since heat is conserved separately in each body

103. Sublimation refers to a change of state where a substance goes directly from: A) Solid to gas (or gas to solid) without passing through the liquid phase B) Liquid to gas C) Solid to liquid D) Gas to liquid only

104. The specific latent heat of a substance depends on: A) The nature of the substance and the type of phase change (fusion or vaporization) B) The mass of the substance only C) The container shape D) The color of the substance

105. Heat capacity (thermal capacity) of a body is: A) The product of its mass and specific heat capacity (heat needed to raise its temperature by 1 K) B) The same as specific heat capacity, regardless of mass C) Independent of the mass of the body D) Measured in units of joules per kilogram only

106. Why does sweating cool the human body (an everyday application of latent heat)? A) Evaporating sweat absorbs latent heat of vaporization from the skin, cooling it B) Sweat itself is naturally cold C) Sweat increases the specific heat capacity of skin D) Sweat reflects sunlight away from the body

107. A substance that has a low specific heat capacity, when supplied a given quantity of heat, will show: A) A larger rise in temperature than a substance with high specific heat B) A smaller rise in temperature C) No rise in temperature D) A rise in temperature independent of heat supplied
108. The heat energy Q required to change the state of mass m of a substance (without temperature change) is: A) Q = mL, where L is the specific latent heat B) Q = mcΔθ C) Q = mgh D) Q = ½mv²

109. Ice at 0°C is more effective at cooling a drink than the same mass of water at 0°C because: A) Melting ice absorbs additional latent heat of fusion from the drink B) Ice has a lower density than water C) Ice is colder in temperature than 0°C water D) Ice contains air bubbles that insulate the drink
